case.paper_title: Human Capital and Development Accounting: New Evidence from Wage Gains at Migration
case.focal_claim: ... immigrants who have never been to high school gain ... more on migration to the United States than immigrants with a college degree (p. 682.)
case.hypothesis: Among immigrants in the authorized wage-gain data, the log wage gain from the last home-country job to the last U.S. job is larger for immigrants with no high school education than for immigrants with a college degree.

tasks_info.task_instruction: In Task 1, the analyst was asked to conduct the analysis without any restrictions.
tasks_info.task_goal: Test whether the focal claim is supported.

tasks_info.task_instruction: You should use the pooled sample of immigrants from poor countries in the NIS (New Immigrant Survey) and the Migration Projects, including Mexico. You should not control for sector: agriculture/nonagriculture, and region i.e. whether an immigrant grew up in a rural or an urban area.
tasks_info.task_goal: Produce one statistical result comparable to the original paper's focal result.

datasets.authorized_only: true. No agent may substitute a dataset not listed here.
datasets.source_type: Survey/archive data from immigrant wage histories in the New Immigrant Survey and Migration Projects as represented in the authorized wage-gain table.
datasets.wave_or_subset: Authorized pooled wage_gain_table.xlsx file; the task-specific instruction identifies it as the pooled poor-country NIS and Migration Projects sample including Mexico.
datasets.sample_size: 2854 rows observed in the authorized dataset before analytic exclusions.
datasets.notes: The authorized dataset contains adjusted pre- and post-migration hourly wages, education years, country, sex, birth year, job years, and home/U.S. occupation groups. No rural/urban region variable is present. Adjusted wage variables are positive in the inspected dataset but are still checked before log transformation. lastHomeWageAdjusted has a very large maximum, motivating the planned median-regression robustness path.

plan.path_summary: Estimate the focal no-high-school versus college-degree difference in immigrant log wage gains using median quantile regression as a robustness analysis to the prior OLS paths, motivated by the extreme adjusted-wage values in the authorized dataset. Task1 uses available demographic, country, and timing controls; Task2 uses the pooled poor-country sample including Mexico with no sector or region controls.

path_signature.sample_restriction: Use authorized wage_gain_table.xlsx rows with nonmissing required variables and positive adjusted home and U.S. wages; Task2 treats the file as the instructed pooled poor-country sample and retains Mexico.
path_signature.missing_data_rule: Listwise deletion on required raw variables and constructed model variables; drop nonpositive adjusted wages before log transformation.
path_signature.variable_construction: Compute log_wage_gain as log(lastUsWageAdjusted) minus log(lastHomeWageAdjusted); construct edu_group from edyrs with no_high_school <= 8, some_high_school 9-11, high_school_some_college 12-15, and college_degree >= 16; construct Task1 age_home_job as yearLastHomeJob - yrborn and its square.
path_signature.inference_rule: A positive no_high_school coefficient relative to college_degree is support; p < 0.05 indicates strong statistical evidence, while p >= 0.05 with a positive estimate is weak directional support. A negative estimate is inconclusive unless it provides affirmative contrary evidence such as p < 0.05 and a confidence interval excluding zero in the negative direction.

analysis_path.path_description: Run a median quantile regression of log wage gain on education groups, using college degree as the reference and estimating the no-high-school contrast while adjusting for country, sex, age at last home job, age squared, and last home/U.S. job years.
preprocessing_steps: Read data/wage_gain_table.xlsx.
Report starting row count.
Verify the required columns edyrs, yearLastHomeJob, yearLastUsJob, sex, yrborn, country, lastHomeWageAdjusted, and lastUsWageAdjusted exist.
Drop rows missing required raw variables and report removals.
Drop rows with nonpositive lastHomeWageAdjusted or lastUsWageAdjusted and report removals.
Compute log_wage_gain = log(lastUsWageAdjusted) - log(lastHomeWageAdjusted).
Construct edu_group from edyrs: no_high_school if edyrs <= 8, some_high_school if 9 <= edyrs < 12, high_school_some_college if 12 <= edyrs < 16, college_degree if edyrs >= 16.
Construct age_home_job = yearLastHomeJob - yrborn and age_home_job_sq = age_home_job^2.
Drop rows missing constructed model variables and report removals.
Fit q = 0.5 quantile regression with college_degree as the reference education group.
Report the no_high_school versus college_degree coefficient, p-value, confidence interval, exponentiated percent difference, sample flow, final analytic N, and education group counts.

key_choices.outlier_rule: No deletion or winsorization of outliers; median regression is used to reduce sensitivity to extreme wage-gain observations while keeping the authorized sample.
key_choices.missing_data_rule: Listwise deletion on required raw and constructed model variables.
key_choices.data_processing: Compute log wage gain and education categories; construct age at last home job and age squared; no aggregation.
key_choices.inference_rule: An estimate in the expected positive direction is support; it is strong support when p < 0.05 and weak or directional support otherwise. Opposite requires affirmative evidence of a material negative effect; an opposite-signed estimate alone is inconclusive.

models.formula: log_wage_gain ~ C(edu_group, Treatment(reference="college_degree")) + C(country) + C(sex) + age_home_job + age_home_job_sq + yearLastHomeJob + yearLastUsJob
models.planned_estimation: Coefficient for no_high_school relative to college_degree in the conditional median of log_wage_gain.
models.inference_criteria: Positive coefficient supports the focal claim; p < 0.05 describes strong statistical evidence; positive but p >= 0.05 is weak directional support; a negative coefficient is inconclusive unless p < 0.05 and the 95% confidence interval is fully negative.
models.qualification: The focal claim is about gaining more on migration, and the authorized data contain extreme adjusted wages. Median regression estimates the same education contrast on the same log wage-gain scale while reducing sensitivity to extreme values without deleting observations.

outcome.variable_construction: log(lastUsWageAdjusted) - log(lastHomeWageAdjusted), after requiring both adjusted wage variables to be positive.
outcome.missing_data_handling: Rows missing either adjusted wage or with nonpositive adjusted wages are excluded.
